name: GraphQL Design
description: GraphQL — schema-first design, proper nullability, cursor pagination, N+1 prevention, error handling
content:
# GraphQL Design Rules

- Design schema-first — define your GraphQL schema before writing resolvers, and use it as the contract between frontend and backend
- Make fields non-null by default — only use nullable fields when null has a meaningful semantic (e.g., optional profile photo)
- Implement cursor-based pagination with the Connection pattern (`edges`, `node`, `pageInfo`) — avoid offset-based pagination for large datasets
- Prevent N+1 queries with DataLoader — batch and cache database lookups within a single request lifecycle
- Use union types and interfaces for polymorphic fields — avoid stringly-typed `type` fields with conditional resolution
- Return structured errors in the `errors` array with extensions for error codes — never expose internal stack traces to clients
- Use input types (`input`) for mutations — keep mutation arguments grouped and documented in a single input object
- Name mutations as verb-noun pairs (`createUser`, `updatePost`) and return the mutated object plus a success/error status
- Apply field-level authorization in resolvers — never rely solely on query-level auth since clients control which fields they request
- Keep resolvers thin — delegate business logic to service layers and use resolvers only for data fetching and field mapping
